display.purpose: The one page headline, about 12ch per line, balanced over two lines.

title.purpose: Step titles and item headings inside a section.

lead.purpose: Hero lead in Steel Gray, about 42ch.

lead-section.purpose: Section leads in Steel Gray, about 32ch.

reading.purpose: Short explanatory paragraphs in Steel Gray, about 34ch.

action.purpose: Labels in action rows; lesson titles.

meta.purpose: Stage labels, level numbers, switch labels, licence line.

label.purpose: Status tags and lesson numbers, tabular figures.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: Outline for neutral status tags and unpressed toggles. Reads as a hairline, not depth.

shadows.name: signal-ring
shadows.purpose: Outline for step numerals, In progress tags and pressed toggles.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing, for every transition and entrance.

motion.name: word-reveal
motion.value: blur(10px) to 0, opacity 0 to 1, translateY(0.12em) to 0; 1.1s per word, 38ms stagger; fires 8% inside the viewport

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Secondary content after a title, on a delay.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Disables every reveal, entrance and figure animation; figures stay readable when static.

figureTheme.purpose: Anatomy kit light theme cooled to the canvas. Figures only, never interface tokens.

narrative.overview:
The course runs on the Augen Pro system from Refero, carried over through Duke Azeta's portfolio: one face at one weight (PP Neue Montreal Book, 350, with ss01 and ss02 on), a cool off-white canvas, near-black ink, one Signal Blue that only ever draws text and thin outlines, 0.5px hairlines instead of shadows, and a lot of empty space. Words carry the page.

The layout is the owner's own, not augen.pro's page structure. Everything sits on a centred axis: headline, lead, actions and figure stack down the middle, and long lists (the method steps, the roadmap) sit in narrow centred columns. Type runs a step larger than the Refero ramp, so a page reads calm and big rather than dense. Sections alternate between canvas and surface, which is the only way a page changes tone. There are no cards, no coloured bands and no chips.

Lessons need to show ideas, so the only imagery is the interactive isometric figures made with the anatomy skill. Each figure is a machine the reader can switch on. Around them, the interface stays flat and text-first. Headings and leads resolve from blur word by word as they come into view; that is the one entrance move.
keyCharacteristics: One weight (350) of one face for everything, nothing bolder.
Centred axis, big type, narrow centred lists.
Canvas and surface alternate by section; nothing else carries colour.
Signal Blue as link text and 0.5px outlines only.
0.5px hairlines and inset rings; no shadows.
Anatomy figures are the only pictures.
Blur-in word reveal on headings and leads.

rules.name: The Signal Is Never a Fill Rule
rules.body: In the interface, Signal Blue is text colour, a 0.5px ring or a focus outline. It never fills a button, tag, section or block. The one exception lives inside a figure, where a depicted interface part (Fig 0's clicked button) may be filled blue because the figure is showing a real page.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: A page changes tone only by switching a whole section between canvas and surface. No coloured bands, dark bands or gradient backgrounds.

rules.name: The Inverted Selection Rule
rules.body: Selected text is an ink background with surface text.

rules.name: The Figure Palette Rule
rules.body: Figures use the anatomy kit's light theme cooled to the canvas: page and card on canvas, faces and tops on surface, four cool shades (#d9d9de to #f2f2f5) for volume, ink steps for edges and text. Signal Blue may mark the one moving or active part. No other hue enters a figure unless the concept needs it, and then it is recorded here.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Everything is set at 350. No bold, no italic, no weight above 400; `font-synthesis: none` stays on.

rules.name: The Step Larger Rule
rules.body: The landing ramp sits one step above the Refero ramp (hero to 5.25rem, section titles to 3.75rem, leads to 1.625rem, step titles to 1.875rem). New pages start from these sizes, not the smaller Refero ones.

rules.name: The Blur-In Rule
rules.body: Headings and leads arrive word by word from a 10px blur (1.1s per word, 38ms stagger, 0.12em rise) when they enter the viewport. Text renders fully visible until the script arms it, and nothing moves under prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every edge is 0.5px. If a boundary needs more weight, move it to hairline-strong, not to a thicker line or a shadow.

dos: Do set every piece of text in PP Neue Montreal at 350 with ss01 and ss02 on.
Do centre the page's axis and keep lists in narrow centred columns (44rem for long lists, 38rem for stacks).
Do start type from the step-larger ramp: display up to 5.25rem, section titles up to 3.75rem, leads up to 1.625rem.
Do alternate whole sections between canvas (#f2f2f4) and surface (#fdfdfd).
Do use the tinted capsule for the one primary action on a view, with a Signal Blue text link beside it for the secondary.
Do draw edges as 0.5px hairlines or inset 0.5px rings.
Do reveal headings and leads word by word from blur, and gate every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion.
Do keep one anatomy figure per lesson, in the light theme cooled to the canvas.
Do write copy plainly, run it through the humanizer, and never use em dashes.
donts: Don't use weights above 400, bold or italic.
Don't fill any interface element with Signal Blue.
Don't set text in Faint Gray (#8f8f8f).
Don't add drop shadows, glows or gradients to the interface.
Don't use cards, coloured or dark bands, or decorative chips; status tags and figure toggles are the only small pills.
Don't copy augen.pro's page structure: no pill nav, scroll pill or two-line label columns.
Don't add stock illustration, photos or ornamental icons. Functional marks (the disclosure chevron, the GitHub mark) are fine; the anatomy figures are the only pictures.
